chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:
Indeed, religion (debts/obligations) comes before the will, then the will follows religion, then inheritance comes after religion, for the first judgment is the Book of Allah.

key_terms.الْوَصِيَّة: The Will (bequest of up to one-third of estate)
key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: The Book of Allah (Quranic basis for obligations)

ai.seo_question: What is the order of settling debts, wills, and inheritance in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar establishes a precise legal hierarchy for estate settlement, prioritizing general religious obligations (Huquq Allah) over specific bequests (Wasiyyah) and finally inheritance (Mirath). It underscores the principle that the 'Book of Allah' serves as the foundational authority for these judgments, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of divine law through the Imams. This ordering ensures that spiritual debts are cleared before worldly distribution, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence (Fiqh).
